---
title: Get started
description: Install MCP Console, connect an MCP client, and run your first analysis.
---

MCP Console runs on the same host as your MCP client.
For remote work, run the client and Console together on that host, alongside the client's shell and filesystem tools.

## Install

Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/).
To use R, install it with [rig](https://github.com/r-lib/rig#id-installation) and run `rig add release`.
Python and SQL also work without R.

Source installation requires Git, [rustup](https://rustup.rs/) with Rust 1.95 or later, and platform build tools.
On macOS, run:

```sh
xcode-select --install
```

On Ubuntu:

```sh
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y build-essential git pkg-config libcap-dev libcurl4-openssl-dev binutils
```

For Windows, follow the [Windows build and installation guide](WINDOWS.md#build-and-run).

Install Console and its private sandbox runner:

```sh
uv tool install git+https://github.com/t-kalinowski/mcp-console
```

Installation builds the pinned sandbox runner with its own toolchain.
Initial runtime preparation can download interpreters, packages, and extensions.
The [release guide](../RELEASE.md#private-sandbox-executable) lists the build prerequisites.

## Connect your client

Configure your MCP client to launch `uvx mcp-console serve` over stdio.
For clients that use an `mcpServers` configuration:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "console": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["mcp-console", "serve"]
    }
  }
}
```

The [repository quickstart](../README.md#quickstart) includes commands for individual clients.
Confirm that your client exposes the `send` tool.

Without R, Console uses `uv` to select Python.
To use an existing project environment, set `python: .venv/bin/python` in `.agents/console/config.yaml`; that environment's packages must already be installed.
See [configuration](CONFIGURATION.md#python-environment-selection) for selection rules and Windows paths.

## Try an analysis

Ask your agent:

> Use MCP Console to explore the Palmer Penguins data from the R package `palmerpenguins`.
> Fit a logistic regression in R to predict penguin sex from body measurements, summarize the data by species with SQL, and plot the model's predictions with Python and Matplotlib.
> Keep the data and model for follow-up.

Then ask:

> Where does the model make the most mistakes?
> Show me a plot and the path to the recorded session transcript.

For a Python-only session, ask Console to generate and analyze a small simulated dataset with NumPy and pandas.
